I like the bump idea. It’s useful for continuing discussion, like in traditional forums. It’s less useful for pushing a constant flow of top-level content, which was reddit’s model for sorting.

There was also a previous suggestion for sorting by number of comments; I can’t find the post, but here’s the Github issue. I think sorting by recent comment activity is more useful (or we could have both).

It could be named “Recently Active” or just “Active”, so the top bar would look like: Hot | New | Active | Top

For now I like sorting by New instead of relying on the Hot queue.

I disagree somewhat with grid view. Grids are good for images but not for titles.

If the goal is to show more threads at once, a “compact” view that is still one thread per line would be better for reading / skimming.

The compact view could collapse all the metadata under the post (time, submitter, all the links etc.) and show ~50 posts instead of 25 per page, with much smaller margins between posts. See mail clients like Gmail’s Display Density setting.

Or again, maybe we could have both. Grid view can be nice for image-centric subs like /v/pics.

Btw, in the future have only one idea per post or it’s hard for others to vote and discuss both separately.

The problem is that with sites like reddit or voat, threads would be bumped every second so basically the same threads that are on the front page would also be on the bumped page. Just go to /r/askreddit, count the amount of replies to each thread and then refresh. They'll very likely have changed.
